title: Mirabel and the Spire
premise: Jonah Kavanagh was exiled from Thornfell for a storm he didn't call — a storm that killed the royal line and left the country a nameless ruin ruled by the Church of the Silence. When the old gods stir again and begin granting prayers in the mountains, the Church hunts every worshipper, and Jonah is dragged back to protect the last priestess, Wren, who carries a god's dying spark. Their escape route lies through the Spire, a tower that once anchored Thornfell's borders and now stands half in this world and half out. To open its door, Wren must give the spark back to the god — erasing herself — unless Jonah can convince the god that a mortal life is worth more than a restored border. In the end, the god chooses to die instead, freeing Wren, and Jonah chooses exile again — but this time with someone beside him.
about_author: Mirabel Kavanagh is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about borders, both the kind drawn on maps and the kind drawn around hearts.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. On a rain-slick pass, Jonah smuggles medicine past Church wardens and hears, for the first time in ten years, a prayer answered out loud. The old gods are waking. Emotional beat: wary wonder — the country he was exiled from is changing without him.

chapters.title: What the Silence Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A young priestess of the Silence tends a chapel that no longer answers, until the god she serves whispers her name and presses a dying spark into her hands. Emotional beat: terror and awe as duty becomes something alive and burning.

chapters.title: Wardens on the White Road
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Church wardens burn a mountain village hunting the spark-bearer. Jonah, who swore never to go back for anyone, breaks his own rule and pulls a half-frozen Wren from the smoke. Emotional beat: the cost of an old instinct for rescue.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Exile
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Hiding in a smuggler's cave, Jonah tells Wren about the storm that killed Thornfell's royal line and the exile that followed. She doesn't believe he called it. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a man carrying a lie that isn't his.

chapters.title: The Spark Speaks
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The god inside Wren dreams aloud — fragments of the Spire, a door, a border that must be closed before Thornfell dissolves entirely. The Church's hounds close in. Emotional beat: love for a god that may be asking her to die.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Salt
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah bargains with a smuggler-queen for passage, paying with the one thing he has left: his true name, which the Church has a price on. Emotional beat: the quiet erosion of what exile was supposed to protect.

chapters.title: The Chapel at Kestrel Ford
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In a ruined chapel, Wren heals a dying child with the spark — a small miracle the Church will call heresy. Jonah watches and understands what he's protecting. Emotional beat: first tenderness between them, unspoken.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. The Church's inquisitor, Brother Hale, corners them at a river crossing. Jonah calls a storm to cover their escape — the same storm-shape as the one that damned him. Emotional beat: horror at becoming, again, the weapon they say he is.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw in the Storm
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. In the storm's eye, the god shows Wren the truth: the royal line was killed by the Church itself, and Jonah was the scapegoat. Emotional beat: fury, and the terrible weight of knowing something Jonah doesn't.

chapters.title: The Lie Between Them
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Wren almost tells him the truth and doesn't. Jonah catches the hesitation and assumes the worst — that she'll trade him to the Church for safe passage. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking under the pressure of withheld truth.

chapters.title: The Ascent to Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. They climb into the dead heart of Thornfell, past villages where prayers are being answered and worshippers are being burned for it. Emotional beat: a country remembering itself, beautiful and doomed.

chapters.title: Brother Hale's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Hale captures Wren alone and offers her a deal: the spark for Jonah's life. She refuses — and realizes she has chosen a man over her god. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided in a single breath.

chapters.title: The Prison Beneath the Spire
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah surrenders himself to buy Wren's freedom and finds the Church's cells full of answered prayers — gods, caged. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Hale interrogates Jonah and reveals the truth of the storm — the Church killed the royals and needed an exile to blame. Jonah's ten years of guilt collapse. Emotional beat: grief for a decade spent carrying someone else's crime.

chapters.title: The Spark Descends
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Wren walks into the Spire to give the spark back and close the border, believing it will erase her. The god, dying, tells her it never wanted a sacrifice. Emotional beat: devotion meeting its limit.

chapters.title: The Door That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The Spire opens onto a country that isn't on any map — Thornfell as it was, or as it remembers being. To leave, they must find a door out of something that has already ended. Emotional beat: vertigo, wonder, urgency.

chapters.title: Storm Against Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Hale and his wardens storm the Spire. Jonah, no longer hiding what he is, calls a true storm for the first time — and it answers him like it never did before. Emotional beat: reclamation of a stolen identity.

chapters.title: The God's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. At the border's anchor, the god must choose: restore Thornfell with Wren's life, or die and let the country go. It chooses to die, spending its last spark to hold the door open for them. Emotional beat: heartbreak and grace.

chapters.title: The Falling of the Spire
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. The Spire comes down; Hale is buried by the country he tried to silence. Jonah carries Wren out through the last door as Thornfell's name fades from the world. Emotional beat: survival that feels like loss.

chapters.title: After the Border
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. On the far side, Wren is a priestess of a god who no longer exists, in a country that no longer exists. She grieves, and Jonah stays — not because she needs him, but because she asked. Emotional beat: love without duty holding it up.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Jonah returns to the smuggler-queen to reclaim his name and finds the Church's bounty void — the Silence is collapsing everywhere. He is, for the first time, no one's exile. Emotional beat: freedom that arrives too quietly to trust.

chapters.title: Where Prayers Go Now
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. They walk the smuggler's roads together, and in a small chapel at the edge of the map, someone lights a candle and something — small, new, unnamed — answers. Emotional beat: hope, inherited rather than given.
